Title: The welcome page bug
Repro Steps:
Sometimes when logging in to the system the welcome page shows no division buttons

The login page succeeds and redirects the user to /welcome - this can only mean that any cookie JWT token is still valid - if the token is invalidated then you generally get a 401 back from the check-authentication call and this keeps you on the login page

I think this errors due to the getUserDivisions function starting at line 105 in uses.service.ts - the divisions that a user has access to must only be stored in memory

you can test this theory by signing properly until you get to /welcome with the correct division buttons - then running "taskkill /f /im msedge.exe" - this is the most reliable way to replicate it, closing tabs must keep something in memory, if you have 2 instances of edge running, and close down one, it reopens fine. again, edge must be doing something with the memory and keeping it "live"

When you reload edge and go to the system youll see the blank welcome page

Theres a few workarounds, 
  1. store the divisions in a cookie
  2. store them in local storage
  3. call the getUserDivisons function instead of relying on the variable - kaleida have tried to avoid the overhead from doing this by using the var

We have an access issue with this , it's arisen due to a human error but we need to work around it

If a contact logs in to a company for the first time, they are assigned a main contact on login and this is set in User.SelectedMainContact

If this CONTACT record is deleted, the accompanying field in the User table isnt updated. If the user is then readded on another company with the same email, the User.SelectedMainContact record remains linked to the old contact and when they login they have access to the wrong company.

  1. We could do with a check on login - to ensure the SelectedMainContact still refers to a live contact record
  2. When deleting contacts we need to check if they are linked to a SelectedMainContact field on User and null it

Title: CustomHttpAuthorizeAttribute.AllowClaim
Repro Steps:
This isn't a bug right now, but in the future it may fall down.

The way that we restrict access to cases on the portal is by putting all of the case IDs that a user can access into their token on login (see Constants.CustomClaimTypes.AssociatedClaims), this is fine now, but the cookie limit is less than 4KB and we are currently hitting 1KB on a basic test user. Web browsers tend to start rejecting large cookies as they reach >4KB

The case IDs are saved to the token as a claim in SimpleAuthorizationServerProvider

You can see how they are currently used to govern access in CustomHttpAuthorizeAttribute

It's an easy replacement -
  1. Any endpoints that have "portalCaseClaimId" in the route need work doing on them
  2. Each method needs a new portal specific handler (or IsPortal bool passing like some others do) which governs access to the cases in real time based on the passed user ID and the companies/products/regions/addresses that user has access to

Title: New payment method direct debit
Description:
Add "Total Annual Fee – Monthly – Direct Debit" Payment Method with Threshold-Based Auto-Selection

Summary
Introduce a new payment method - "Total Annual Fee – Monthly – Direct Debit" - and implement automatic selection logic in the service agreement processor so the correct monthly payment method is chosen based on the total service value when a DocuSign is received.

Background / Context Currently, when a DocuSign is processed and monthly payments are selected, the system does not distinguish between customers paying via direct debit and those being financed.
This change introduces a new payment method and routes the selection automatically based on a £10,000 threshold.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. A new payment method "Total Annual Fee – Monthly – Direct Debit" exists and is selectable in the system.
  2.  when the service agreement processor determines the payment method on DocuSign receipt:
    • If monthly payments is selected AND the total amount for service is less than £10,000 -> auto-select "Total Annual Fee – Monthly – Direct Debit"
    • If monthly payments is selected AND the total amount for service is £10,000 or more  -> auto-select "Total Annual Fee – Monthly – Financed" (existing behaviour)
  3. The ESignatureService correctly triggers this selection logic when a DocuSign is received and monthly payments are indicated on the agreement.
  4. No change to behaviour for non-monthly payment types.
  5. The £10,000 threshold is not hard-coded - it should be configurable for future maintainability.

Out of Scope

  • Any changes to the DocuSign template itself
  • Manual override of payment method by staff (separate ticket if needed)
  • Changes to existing "Total Annual Fee – Monthly – Financed" behaviour

Technical Notes

  • Primary expected change points: InvoiceService, ESignatureService==
  • Add unit tests covering:
    • sub-£10k monthly -> direct debit,
    • £10k monthly -> financed, 
    • exactly £10k boundary -> financed, 
    • non-monthly -> unchanged

Definition of Done

  • New payment method added and resolvable by the system
  • Selection logic implemented and unit tested (all 4 cases above)
  • Threshold extracted to a named constant/config
  • Code reviewed and merged
  • Tested against a test DocuSign in staging with a sub-£10k and a £10k+ agreement

Title: Add automated test pipeline to API project
Cover Level not stored for unmatched claims; no validation on link
Description:
Background 

The claims bordereaux contains a required "Cover Level" column (Coverage in the data model). 

When a bordereaux row matches a policy at import time, the Cover Level is validated against that policy and stored. 

When a row is unmatched (no policy found), the Cover Level is currently discarded - it is never persisted to the claim record.

Required changes

  • Store Cover Level on import regardless of match status.
    • When processing a bordereaux row that cannot be matched to a policy, the raw Cover Level value from the file must still be saved against the unmatched claim as a text field (it cannot be resolved to a CoverageId without a policy).
  • Validate Cover Level when linking an unmatched claim to a policy.
    • When UpdateClaimPolicyId() is called, the stored Cover Level value must be checked against the selected policy's configured Coverage options.
    • If valid, resolve it to a CoverageId and store it on the claim as normal.
    • If invalid, return a validation error to the caller so the frontend can prompt the user.
  • Expose the stored Cover Level value on the unmatched claim API response so the frontend can display it.
